discovery: Spectroscopic characterization of exoplanet atmospheres through transmission spectroscopy, including the detection of atomic and molecular species such as sodium and water

nominees.name: David Charbonneau
nominees.affiliation: Harvard University, Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian, USA

motivation: Seager (with Sasselov) showed theoretically that starlight filtered through a transiting planet's limb carries measurable atomic and molecular absorption features. Charbonneau and colleagues then made the first detection of an exoplanet atmosphere, sodium in HD 209458b with Hubble in 2002. Tinetti and collaborators pioneered the identification of molecules, notably water, in hot-Jupiter atmospheres. Together these contributions turned exoplanets from points on a radial-velocity curve into physical worlds whose composition, temperature structure, clouds and chemistry can be measured with quantitative radiative transfer and laboratory molecular data. The method now underpins JWST's precise detections of H2O, CO2, CO, SO2 and CH4, linking the chemistry of planet-forming discs to the atmospheres of mature planets. It is a new observational window that connects fundamental molecular physics to the question of how planets, and eventually habitable conditions, arise.
